decisions.reason: Confirmed a logic gap: the old crossing transversality omitted fold neighborhoods and allowed a fold branch to have an unexamined tangential value crossing with another critical point. Repaired with one finite trigonometric Hermite-jet family on all distinct-point domains. The pair-event Jacobian forces both critical points Morse and the value slopes unequal. The local fold integral excludes diagonal accumulation; compactness then gives finitely many crossings. The simultaneous-event codimensions, endpoint collars, height-only perturbation, embedding openness and stationary-end isotopy extension were checked. The two-event TikZ schematic is mathematically consistent; no Statement change.

Nonfatal citation/interface mismatch: F6 described existence as though it were supplied by the quoted Definition, whose text explicitly reserves that obligation. The current supplier actually discharges it in Proof 3.1. F6 now distinguishes those sections and the conditional Given. The coefficient proof independently gives c0=1 for knots and 0 for multi-component links; smoothing gives the mixed-crossing c1 difference 1, hence the third a2 difference zero and the intersecting/nonintersecting symbol values 1/0. The two cyclic 4T orders cancel, and the Hopf/trefoil skein computations give z and 1+z^2. The two TikZ chord patterns match the values. No Statement or numbered proof change; no Lickorish source reading is claimed in this review.

Confirmed a dependency-citation gap: F5 asserted local ds/s and preceding-long-endpoint estimates absent from its quoted Statement, so mere convergence did not prove the uniform R limit. Repaired F5 and derived the complete fixed-tangle majorant in step 2.2: short factors are C ds/s, fixed long factors C ds, and return factors C ds/(R-M); a surviving short chain has a retained nearer long witness, whose integrated s_k cancels the innermost pole. Keeping one return factor yields a uniform O(1/(R-M)) bound in finitely many bands. For constancy in R, F6 explicitly imports only closed-knot horizontal invariance; regular-piece Stokes computations remain local. Cap 1T, closure of interval diagrams and the oriented connected-sum seam were checked, including both TikZ panels. No Statement change.

Confirmed a logic gap: smooth extension of collision coordinates in F2 does not imply an analytic radial remainder, so the old Taylor recursion did not cover smooth endpoints. Step 3.1 now factors actual branch differences, obtains A/rho+B(rho) with B smooth, and constructs each homogeneous normalized coefficient by an integral from 0. Division by rho is smooth because the preceding positive-degree coefficient vanishes at 0. This gives existence/uniqueness with smooth parameter dependence; nested/disjoint residues commute, permitting the prescribed successive regularizations. The analytic reduced-KZ recurrence, polynomial coefficient bound, constant G1^-1 G0 ratio and noncommutative epsilon limit were checked against the complete CDM §10.1.6 argument. The closure/composition supplier repaired earlier gives hump multiplication; the maxima count and formal inverse give normalization invariance. No Statement change.

Confirmed an ill-typed target: the original Statement placed the truncation in rational diagram modules while the defining series and F5 place its coefficients in their complexifications. The target now explicitly reads the finite direct sum of A_m^un tensor_Q C. This preserves the type bound and exact leading symbol without adding a rationality claim. Linear projection commutes with every finite resolution sum; the associated-graded supplier kills degrees <=n at n+1 singularities and gives exactly D at n singularities, including the unit for n=0. Isotopy invariance retains AC_omega. The only direct item consumer, the universality theorem, already extends weight systems complex-linearly and uses this identical complexified target in its Statement and Proof 1.1–2.1, so it remains sound.

Universality already uses the correct complex-linear target and remains mathematically unchanged.
